title: How to Transfer Large Files Between Android and PC Wirelessly (Faster Than USB 2.0)
html:
When you need to copy a 15 GB 4K video recording or a batch of 800 vacation photos from your Android smartphone to your Windows PC, the default reaction is usually to grab the charging cable that came in your phone's box.

Last updated: 25 Nov 2026. This transfer guide demonstrates how to beam gigabytes of files wirelessly between Android, Windows, and Mac at 50 MB/s to 80 MB/s over local Wi-Fi—completely bypassing slow USB 2.0 cables and buggy MTP drivers.

You plug the cable in, switch the USB connection mode to "File Transfer / MTP", open Windows Explorer, and initiate the copy. Ten seconds later, Windows Explorer hangs, the progress bar freezes, and the transfer fails with a cryptic "The device is unreachable" error. Even when it works, transfer speeds hover between 30 and 40 MB/s.

Here is why traditional USB file transfer on Android is fundamentally broken, and how modern local wireless tools make moving massive files effortless and twice as fast.

The MTP Nightmare: Why Wired USB Transfers Freeze

When you connect an Android phone to a computer via USB, Android does not expose its storage as a standard external drive (mass storage). Instead, it uses Media Transfer Protocol (MTP).

MTP was developed by Microsoft in the early 2000s for MP3 players. Under MTP, Windows cannot read the raw storage filesystem; it must ask Android to package each file individually before transmission. When transferring a folder with 500 small photos, MTP renegotiates permissions for every single photo, causing frequent buffer timeouts.

Combined with the fact that most in-box smartphone cables only carry USB 2.0 data lines (480 Mbps / ~38 MB/s real-world ceiling), wired transfers are literally slower than modern local 5 GHz Wi-Fi.

Method 1: LocalSend (The Open-Source AirDrop Champion)

LocalSend is the cleanest, fastest file-sharing tool ever created for multi-device users. It is 100% free, open-source, requires zero internet connection, and works across Android, Windows, macOS, Linux, and iOS.

  1. Install LocalSend on your Android phone (from Play Store or F-Droid) and on your Windows PC (from localsend.org or Microsoft Store).
  2. Connect both devices to the same home Wi-Fi network (or turn on your phone's Wi-Fi hotspot and connect your laptop to it).
  3. Open LocalSend on both devices. They will automatically discover each other with friendly generated names (e.g., "Fast Avocado" or "Smart Pineapple").
  4. On Android, tap Send → select your files, video clips, or entire folders → tap your PC's name.
  5. On your PC, click Accept. The files will transfer peer-to-peer at speeds reaching 50 MB/s to 85 MB/s, completing a 10 GB transfer in just over two minutes!

Method 2: Google Quick Share for Windows

If you don't want to install third-party utilities on your phone, Google's native Quick Share (formerly Nearby Share) is already built into every Android phone running Android 6.0 and above.

  1. Download and install Quick Share for Windows from the official Android website (android.com/better-together/quick-share-app).
  2. Sign in with your Google account on your PC and toggle device visibility to "Your devices".
  3. On your Android phone, select any photo or video in Google Photos or Files → tap Share → tap Quick Share.
  4. Your Windows PC will appear instantly in the share sheet. Tap it, and the transfer begins automatically via Wi-Fi Direct without prompting for PIN codes.

Which Method Should You Use?

  • Use LocalSend: If you value open-source privacy, transfer files between mixed operating systems (e.g., Android to Mac, or iPhone to Windows), or want zero account logins.
  • Use Quick Share: If you are fully invested in the Google ecosystem and want seamless 1-tap transfers between your Android phone and Windows laptop.

faq.title: Does LocalSend consume internet data when transferring files?
faq.description: No. LocalSend transfers files strictly over your local Wi-Fi router's peer-to-peer network and consumes zero mobile data or internet bandwidth.

faq.title: Why does Windows Explorer freeze when transferring files via USB cable?
faq.description: Android uses MTP (Media Transfer Protocol), which negotiates permissions file-by-file rather than raw disk sectors. When transferring large files or many photos, MTP frequently times out.

faq.title: Can LocalSend transfer files if there is no Wi-Fi router nearby?
faq.description: Yes. Simply turn on your phone's personal Wi-Fi Hotspot, connect your laptop to it, and LocalSend will transfer files at full wireless speeds with zero cellular data needed.
